stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs erase $5.7 billion outflow hole, but profit-taking caps the rebound
stories.summary: Bitcoin ETFs have recovered from a $5.7 billion outflow hole, according to CryptoSlate. New inflows returned, but profit-taking absorbed much of the fresh demand. The rebound looks weaker than the headline recovery number suggests.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key gauge of institutional bitcoin demand, so a capped rebound signals hesitant conviction even after the losses reversed.
whatToWatch: Whether net inflows can outpace profit-taking in coming sessions
Daily ETF flow data for signs of sustained demand
questions: Which funds are seeing the profit-taking, and which are still net buyers?
How much of the $5.7 billion hole reflected speculative versus long-term positioning?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs just erased a $5.7 billion hole, but profit-taking is swallowing the new demand

stories.title: Solana overtakes Ethereum in fees, but Ethereum keeps the burn lead
stories.summary: Solana has surpassed Ethereum in network fees generated, according to CryptoSlate. Ethereum still leads on token burn, the process that removes ETH from supply. The split shows the two networks now lead on different metrics.
stories.whyItMatters: Fee generation and burn rates are core signals of network usage and token supply, both central to long-term valuation debates for SOL and ETH.
whatToWatch: Whether Solana's fee lead holds as usage patterns shift
Ethereum's burn rate relative to new issuance
questions: Is the fee flip driven by activity or by differing fee structures between the chains?

sources.title: Solana flips Ethereum in fees, while ETH holds the burn lead

stories.title: Coin Metrics revises 19 months of ETF wallet data
stories.summary: Coin Metrics has revised 19 months of data tracking bitcoin ETF wallet holdings, according to CryptoSlate. The size of the revision was not detailed in the report. The correction raises questions about how reliable past on-chain ETF tracking has been.
stories.whyItMatters: Traders and analysts rely on ETF wallet data to gauge institutional holdings, so a revision spanning over a year of history could change how past flow narratives are read.
whatToWatch: Coin Metrics' explanation of what drove the revision
Whether other data providers issue similar corrections
questions: How much did the revised figures change from the original data?
Which specific ETFs or wallets were most affected?

sources.title: Coin Metrics revises 19 months of ETF wallet data but by how much?

stories.title: Solana pushes Alpenglow upgrade to testnet as SOL nears January highs
stories.summary: Solana has moved its Alpenglow upgrade into testnet, according to CryptoSlate. The move comes as SOL's price nears its January highs. Alpenglow is a proposed change to Solana's consensus mechanism.
stories.whyItMatters: A consensus-layer upgrade reaching testnet is a concrete step toward mainnet rollout, and the timing next to a price recovery raises the stakes for a clean launch.
whatToWatch: Testnet results and any bugs found before a mainnet date is set
Whether SOL breaks through its January highs
questions: What is the target mainnet date for Alpenglow?
What specific improvements does Alpenglow bring over Solana's current consensus?

stories.title: Why Mastercard's $25 billion crypto expansion isn't what it seems
stories.summary: Mastercard has expanded its crypto business to a reported $25 billion scale, according to CryptoSlate. The report argues the expansion is less significant than the headline figure suggests. The specific caveats behind that claim were not detailed in the supplied title.
stories.whyItMatters: Mastercard's crypto push is often cited as proof of mainstream payment-rail adoption, so a skeptical read on the real substance behind the number matters for gauging genuine institutional uptake.
whatToWatch: Further detail on what the $25 billion figure actually measures
Mastercard's next disclosed crypto product or partnership

stories.title: Europe's central banks push to scrap a stablecoin reserve safeguard
stories.summary: European central banks want to remove a specific safeguard that governs stablecoin reserves, according to CryptoSlate. The push comes amid a wider debate over how stablecoin issuers must back their tokens. The report does not name which safeguard is targeted.
stories.whyItMatters: Reserve rules underpin stablecoin safety, so a central bank push to loosen them could reshape issuer requirements across the EU's MiCA framework.
whatToWatch: Formal proposals from EU central banks on reserve rule changes
Response from stablecoin issuers operating under MiCA
questions: Which safeguard is being targeted, and why?
Would removing it increase or reduce systemic risk?

stories.title: EU central banks push back on MiCA, citing stablecoin run risk
stories.summary: EU central banks are criticizing parts of the MiCA stablecoin rulebook, according to CryptoSlate, and point to stablecoin runs as their justification. The report links this criticism to a related push on reserve requirements. Specifics of any proposed rule changes were not detailed in the supplied title.
stories.whyItMatters: MiCA is the EU's flagship crypto framework, and central bank pushback on its stablecoin provisions could signal a broader regulatory rethink just as the rules take hold.
whatToWatch: Any formal MiCA amendment proposals from EU authorities
Data or examples cited to support the stablecoin run concern
questions: What run event or risk is prompting this pushback?

stories.title: Coinbase traces $1.1 million crypto trail behind AI phishing service EvilTokens
stories.summary: Coinbase investigators traced roughly $1.1 million in crypto tied to an AI-powered phishing service called EvilTokens, according to CryptoSlate. The service reportedly used AI tools to run phishing operations against crypto users. Details on victims and any law enforcement action were not given in the supplied title.
stories.whyItMatters: AI-assisted phishing tools lower the bar for scammers targeting crypto holders, so exchange-led tracing efforts like this one help expose and disrupt new attack patterns.
whatToWatch: Whether law enforcement acts against the EvilTokens operators
Further disclosures on how the service used AI
questions: Who were the victims, and how were they targeted?

stories.title: Bitcoin faces $16 billion options expiry Friday, with two more tests ahead
stories.summary: Bitcoin markets face a $16 billion options expiry on Friday, according to CryptoSlate. The report says two further tests could challenge the current rally after that. Large expiries can add short-term volatility as positions unwind.
stories.whyItMatters: Expiries of this size can swing bitcoin's price sharply in the short term, so readers tracking the rally will want to know if it holds through the pressure points ahead.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin's price action around Friday's expiry
The two additional tests flagged for the rally
questions: What are the two additional tests specifically?

stories.title: Altcoin demand faces $18 billion threat as flows shift to RWA perps
stories.summary: Altcoin demand is under pressure from an $18 billion threat, according to CryptoSlate, as trading flows move toward real-world-asset (RWA) perpetual futures. The report says only 19% of traders currently hold altcoin positions. The shift points to narrowing speculative interest beyond bitcoin and a few large-cap assets.
stories.whyItMatters: A shrinking share of traders holding altcoins signals weaker market breadth, which matters for anyone judging whether gains are broad-based or concentrated in a few assets.
whatToWatch: Whether RWA perp volumes keep growing at altcoins' expense
Any rebound in the share of traders holding altcoin positions
questions: What exactly makes up the $18 billion threat figure?
Which RWA perp products are drawing the flows?

sources.title: Altcoin demand meets $18B threat as flows move into RWA perps as just 19% of traders keep alts
